blocks.explains: When an archive advertises: on a sealed bucket, a fixed interval, AIMD, or both.
Spread applied to bucket-close under global numbering, where every archive seals the same bucket at the same moment and fires together.
How two archives settle a disagreement - send a sketch, enumerate, or sketch then fall back. Delivery should not move; what it costs should.
How many differences one sketch can decode before it fails and the exchange escalates.
Whether the advert carries its 66-byte signature.
Sketch member width. Narrower identifiers collide more often, and a collision cancels in the sketch without cancelling in the checksum.
The same nominal loss delivered in 60-second stretches of deafness, which puts a whole bucket's divergence into one sketch instead of spreading it.
Every node rebroadcasting everything, against a real role census.
Hop limits past anything a release ships, to find where more hops stop helping.
A flat loss floor on every reception - degradation spread evenly across every bucket.
Burst loss at half an hour rather than a minute - most of a bucket, which is the outage that actually matters to an archive.
Transmit power in dBm - the region limit is a ceiling an operator may use, not one they must.
flags: faster: 1.06 s per simulated hour against 2.33 over 3 prior run(s) - 2.2x quicker, which is worth a look: a fragmented mesh or an arm that stopped being read both cost less to simulate

blocks.explains: Every router as an archive against half of them - same mesh, same traffic, only who holds the archive changes.
How many hops apart the archives are placed, under a flat hop limit.
Where the archives sit, under a flat hop limit.
How many archives the mesh has, under a flat hop limit.
What defines a bucket: a global counter (a fiction kept as an upper bound), the local count the firmware keeps, a time window, or a sliding window.
Width of the time bucket, when buckets are cut by the clock.
Sketch capacity under windowed buckets rather than counted ones.
Objects in the sliding window, when buckets are windowed.
The same node counts in a fixed area, so this is density rather than size. Running both is the only way to say which an effect belongs to.
One hop limit for everyone, swept. The per-node spread must be off or --hop-limit is never read.
Mesh size with density held constant - the area grows with the node count.
A uniform hop limit against per-node limits of 3-7 assigned by centrality.
Whether an archive advertises by broadcast or by DM to each known peer.
Whether a replay goes by DM or by broadcast, so bystanders in earshot can file it too.
Sketch capacity under local numbering and the later defaults.
The same, with replays broadcast - the combination the replay header exists for.
Advert spread under local numbering, where each archive seals its own bucket on its own count and the synchronisation jitter would break is largely absent.
Where a replayed object lands in the receiver's stream: at the tip, or back at its heard_ago.
How many hops apart the archives are, under real per-node hop limits.
Where the archives sit, under real per-node hop limits.
How many archives the mesh has, under real per-node hop limits.
Spreading factor with bandwidth held at 500 kHz, where North America is heading.
The quiet-hours window reconciliation defers to, which only means anything once traffic has a time of day.
The firmware's node-count interval scaling, on against off.
flags: no-congestion-scaling=True: queue drops 16.4% of transmissions - airtime here is measured through a cap

blocks.explains: Time of day. Text, position and DMs follow the clock; telemetry and nodeinfo are device timers and do not.
The presets Europe runs, including the narrow ones EU_866 and EU_N_868 default to.
The presets deployed meshes actually run: the default, the fast end, and the slow end still in use.
The same nodes in the same places with the archive off then on, separating what serving costs a node from where it sits.
Whether raised hop limits land on central nodes as operators do it, or at random - the control that separates the limit's effect from the siting of the nodes that raised it.
The device broadcast interval - the denominator every SF++ airtime share is quoted against.
Nothing, the incumbent chain walk, and the sketch - with `none` a paired baseline, so every other cell is a difference rather than a comparison.
The shape of the mesh, at fixed node count and seed.
The hop-recommendation feedback loop closed against held open, traced, because a converged mean and an oscillating one look identical at the end.
Which quantity drives the throttle: what the firmware can see and which saturates, or the unbounded ideal.
Each node throttling on its own online count against one coefficient for the whole mesh. The firmware does the former.
Raising the coding rate on each retransmission - airtime spent to make each attempt likelier to land.
How a DM escalates to flooding.
DM escalation with the coding-rate ladder already on, since both spend the same retry budget.
Router-like nodes favouriting each other, so relays between them keep their hop limit.
The pre-fold-in transport against 2.8 - same seed, same mesh, only the MAC and routing rules change.
flags: slower: 7.35 s per simulated hour against 1.93 over 3 prior run(s) - 3.8x, and a runtime regression is invisible to `timeout-minutes` until it fails a job outright

blocks.explains: How far the firmware's hop estimator sits from the exhaustive count it approximates, as the mesh outgrows its 128 entries.
The modelled MAX_NUM_NODES - the size of the hot store.
The store size against a fixed 250-node mesh, so eviction is constant.
A mesh part-way through upgrading, the older share on 2.5.
The same with the older share on 2.6.

blocks.explains: Mesh size against a store that has to hold it, over a full day.
The board mix, which decides each node's hot-store size.
The rebroadcast mode - what a node relays.
The cheapest rival to an archive: one extra relay of a text rather than replicating it afterwards.
The same, on a mesh busy enough for the suppression thresholds to be deciding it.
The legacy default role census against a real mesh's.
The same with router favourites on.
The share of nodes on ROUTER_LATE.
The receive-side signature policy - what a node does with an unsigned packet.
Signing itself, on against off inside 2.8. The only arm that separates 'signing costs reach' from '2.8 costs reach'.
Where nodes physically are. A roof node and a basement one are 26 dB apart, wider than most parameters here.
Retries per addressed reconciliation hop, to find where delivery stops improving.
Route discoveries per node per hour - whether traceroute learning pays for its own airtime.
The same on a mesh whose hot store cannot hold it, where the overflow cache is all that keeps a route for the long tail.

The same, with every node on a flat hop limit of 7 so nothing damps the flood.

Every distance scaled about the centroid: the same nodes in the same arrangement, further apart.
